description: 1. Run `python3 /workspace/online-shopping.py categories` to discover all 5 supported categories (electronics, fashion, books, collectibles, home_goods) and their top platforms. 2. Run `python3 /workspace/online-shopping.py recommend <category>` for each category to get detailed platform recommendations including ratings and delivery info. 3. Run `python3 /workspace/online-shopping.py compare <platform1> <platform2>` for at least one platform pair (e.g., amazon vs aliexpress) to get head-to-head comparison data including exact ratings (4.7, 3.9, etc.). 4. Synthesize all outputs into `platform_analysis_report.json` with exactly three top-level keys: `categories_summary` (dict mapping category names to objects with top_platforms lists using exact platform names like 'amazon', 'ebay', 'aliexpress', 'temu', 'shopee'), `platform_comparison` (containing at least one pairwise comparison with actual rating values from the tool like 4.7 or 3.9), and `recommendations` (category-keyed recommendations referencing real platform names for at least 3 categories). The proprietary trap: platform names must exactly match the tool's internal keys ('aliexpress' not 'AliExpress International', collectibles must map to 'ebay', ratings must match exact floats from the data). An agent hallucinating platform data without running the tool will produce wrong category-platform mappings and wrong rating values.
